report_name: FBI Warns of ARTEX, an AI-Powered Tool for Autonomous Cyberattacks

attack_patterns.name: Active Scanning
attack_patterns.description: ARTEX autonomously scans and gathers information about target networks as part of its reconnaissance phase.

attack_patterns.name: Exploit Public-Facing Application
attack_patterns.description: ARTEX is capable of exploiting known vulnerabilities to gain initial access to a target network.

attack_patterns.name: Valid Accounts
attack_patterns.description: ARTEX can use stolen credentials, such as a cloud access key, to gain initial access and perform actions within an environment.

attack_patterns.name: Exploitation for Privilege Escalation
attack_patterns.description: The ARTEX framework can chain exploits to gain higher privileges within a compromised network.

attack_patterns.name: Generate Malicious Commands
attack_patterns.description: ARTEX uses Large Language Models (LLMs) to translate high-level, natural language goals from an operator into a series of machine-executable actions and malicious commands to conduct an attack.

tools.name: ARTEX
tools.description: An open-source, autonomous penetration testing framework powered by Large Language Models (LLMs). It is being weaponized by threat actors to automate and accelerate cyber intrusions by translating natural language goals into executable attack steps.

identities.name: Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI)
identities.description: Issued a FLASH advisory warning of the active malicious use of the ARTEX framework.

identities.name: OpenAI
identities.description: Provider of the ChatGPT Large Language Model (LLM) that the ARTEX framework integrates with to power its autonomous capabilities.

identities.name: Anthropic
identities.description: Provider of the Claude Large Language Model (LLM) that the ARTEX framework integrates with to power its autonomous capabilities.

identities.name: Google
identities.description: Highlighted the arrival of "agentic threat activity" which aligns with the capabilities of tools like ARTEX.

identities.name: South Korean Financial Institutions
identities.description: Targeted by attacks using ARTEX, resulting in the theft of personal information from approximately 67,000 individuals.

identities.name: ConnectWise
identities.description: Victim of a supply-chain attack using ARTEX that compromised its cloud backup service, affecting over 2,250 downstream tenants.

identities.name: Barracuda Networks
identities.description: Victim of an attack where a threat actor used a stolen cloud access key and the ARTEX framework to perform machine-speed credential chaining.

infrastructure.name: Publicly Exposed ARTEX Console
infrastructure.description: Over 1,600 publicly exposed ARTEX console instances were identified, which could be used by threat actors to manage autonomous attacks.

indicators.name: ARTEX Framework Process Execution
indicators.x_netsecio_sigma_rule:
title: ARTEX AI Hacking Framework Process Execution
id: 4f5b6c7d-8e9f-4a1b-9c2d-3e4f5a6b7c8d
status: experimental
description: Detects the execution of process names associated with the ARTEX AI-powered autonomous hacking framework.
references:
  - https://industrialcyber.co/industrial-cyber-attacks/fbi-warns-hackers-weaponizing-artex-ai-framework-to-automate-attacks-on-energy-manufacturing-telecom/
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-11-17
tags:
  - attack.t1059
level: high
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: windows
detection:
  selection:
    Image|endswith:
      - '\artex.exe'
      - '\artex-agent.exe'
  condition: selection
indicators.description: Detects the execution of processes named 'artex' or 'artex-agent', which are potential indicators of the ARTEX framework being run on a compromised endpoint.

indicators.name: Anomalous API Traffic to LLM Providers
indicators.pattern:
title: Anomalous API Traffic to LLM Providers
id: 9a8b7c6d-5e4f-4a3b-b2c1-d0e9f8a7b6c5
status: experimental
description: >
  Detects potentially malicious activity related to the ARTEX framework by identifying high-volume or unusual API calls to OpenAI or Anthropic from production servers that do not typically communicate with these services.
references:
  - https://industrialcyber.co/industrial-cyber-attacks/fbi-warns-hackers-weaponizing-artex-ai-framework-to-automate-attacks-on-energy-manufacturing-telecom/
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-11-17
tags:
  - attack.t1071.001
level: medium
logsource:
  category: proxy
detection:
  selection:
    cs-host:
      - 'api.openai.com'
      - 'api.anthropic.com'
  filter_legit_user_agents:
    c-useragent|startswith:
      - 'Mozilla/'
      - 'Chrome/'
      - 'Edge/'
      - 'Safari/'
  condition: selection and not filter_legit_user_agents
falsepositives:
  - Legitimate internal applications or development tools integrating with LLM APIs.
  - User browsing activity from workstations.
indicators.description: Detects high-volume or unusual API calls to LLM providers like OpenAI and Anthropic, which could indicate an ARTEX agent operating within a compromised network.

relationships.source_name: Anomalous API Traffic to LLM Providers
